topic: Klarna's OpenAI-powered AI customer-service assistant (Feb 2024 claims) and the May 2025 pivot back toward human customer service, with later updates through Feb 2026

claims.claim: "Klarna today announced its AI assistant powered by OpenAI." Press release headline: "Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month".

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: The announcement itself is a fact. The release says the assistant was "Now live globally for 1 month", which puts the global launch around late January 2024 (inferred, not stated as a date).

claims.claim: "2.3 million conversations, two-thirds of Klarna's customer service chats" in the first month.

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month
Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service

claims.notes: Unaudited company metric. Counts chats only, not phone or email. Entrepreneur (2025-05-09) says "75%", which conflicts with Klarna's own "two-thirds". Use two-thirds.

claims.claim: "It is doing the equivalent work of 700 full-time agents"

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: This is an FTE-equivalence estimate made by the company. It does not say 700 people were fired. Media headlines such as "Klarna's AI replaced 700 workers" (The Independent, 2025-05-22) are an interpretation. Siemiatkowski said Klarna outsources "the few thousand human agents" it uses, so most agents were not Klarna employees. Avoid saying "fired 700".

claims.claim: "Customers now resolve their errands in less than 2 mins compared to 11 mins previously"

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: Unaudited. The units are minutes per errand (resolution time). The May 2025 spokesperson figure was "response times have improved 82% since launch" (CX Dive), which is a different metric. Do not merge the two.

claims.claim: "It is on par with human agents in regard to customer satisfaction score"; "more accurate errand resolution, leading to a 25% drop in repeat inquiries"

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: No CSAT number was published. Siemiatkowski's May 2025 "lower quality" remark is in tension with the "on par" claim.

claims.claim: Available "in 23 markets, 24/7" and "communicates in more than 35 languages"

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: This is product scope as Klarna described it.

claims.claim: "It's estimated to drive a $40 million USD in profit improvement to Klarna in 2024"

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: This was a forward-looking company estimate. I did not find an audited figure confirming that $40M was realized in 2024.

claims.claim: "Additionally, customers can still choose to interact with live agents if they'd prefer."

sources.title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month

claims.notes: This is an important nuance: a human option existed in the original 2024 announcement, so the 2025 pivot was not literally "bringing back the option to reach a human". It was about investing in in-house human quality.

claims.claim: Siemiatkowski said Klarna stopped hiring about a year earlier as it invested in AI, and headcount fell 22% to about 3,500, mostly through attrition.

sources.title: Klarna stopped all hiring a year ago to replace workers with AI
Klarna Is Hiring Customer Service Agents After AI Couldn't Cut It on Calls, According to the Company's CEO

claims.notes: Trending Topics noted that Klarna still had job postings, so the freeze was not absolute. Seen in search snippets only; I did not fetch the Fortune article directly.

claims.claim: IPO prospectus: full-time employees fell from 5,527 (end of Dec 2022) to 3,422 (end of Dec 2024). The CEO described it as "from about 5,000 to now almost 3,000 employees" and also said "Natural attrition in a company like ours is 15-20% per year".

sources.title: Klarna CEO says AI helped company shrink workforce by 40%
sources.publisher: CNBC (Annie Palmer), syndicated on NBC New York

sources.title: Profitable Klarna files for a potentially blockbuster IPO

claims.notes: The headcount numbers come from the SEC filing as reported by CNBC. I did not read the F-1 text on sec.gov directly. The headcount drop covers all roles, not just customer service (which was largely outsourced), and the CEO attributes it partly to attrition. The "40%" figure is CNBC's framing of the CEO's rounded numbers. The exact F-1 drop is about 38%.

claims.claim: Siemiatkowski: "As cost unfortunately seems to have been a too predominant evaluation factor when organizing this, what you end up having is lower quality."

sources.title: Klarna Turns From AI to Real Person Customer Service
Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service
Klarna's AI replaced 700 workers. It now wants some of them back to improve customer service

claims.notes: The Bloomberg original is paywalled (HTTP 403), so the quote was verified via two secondary outlets citing Bloomberg, with identical wording. Bloomberg's own summary: the push to cut customer service costs with AI "has gone too far". Treat "has gone too far" as Bloomberg's paraphrase, not a direct quote.

claims.claim: Siemiatkowski: "I just think it's so critical that you are clear to your customer that there will be always a human if you want"

sources.title: Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service
Klarna's AI replaced 700 workers. It now wants some of them back to improve customer service
Klarna Is Hiring Customer Service Agents After AI Couldn't Cut It on Calls, According to the Company's CEO

claims.notes: Word order varies: Entrepreneur has "there will always be a human if you want", while CX Dive and The Independent have "there will be always a human if you want" (the speaker is not a native English speaker). Use the CX Dive/Independent version, or on screen paraphrase it as "always a human if you want".

claims.claim: Siemiatkowski: "Really investing in the quality of the human support is the way of the future for us."

sources.title: Klarna Grapples with AI-Led Customer Service, Pivots to an "Uber Type of Setup"
Klarna's AI replaced 700 workers. It now wants some of them back to improve customer service

claims.notes: Entrepreneur renders it as "investing in the quality of human support" (without "the"). The difference is minor.

claims.claim: Klarna is piloting in-house customer service agents "in an Uber type of setup" (remote, flexible), targeting students, rural populations and passionate Klarna users, aiming eventually to replace some of "the few thousand human agents" it outsources. Only two pilot employees had started at the time of reporting.

sources.title: Klarna's AI replaced 700 workers. It now wants some of them back to improve customer service
Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service
Klarna CEO says AI helped company shrink workforce by 40%

claims.notes: "Rehire" is media framing; I found no evidence that Klarna is rehiring the same people. The Independent says "hire more humans" and "wants some of them back" (headline). It is a pilot that started with two people, not a mass hiring. It is about bringing work in-house from outsourcers, not about reversing AI. The figure of "two" employees comes from secondary reporting (The Independent); I did not verify it against Bloomberg.

claims.claim: Klarna spokesperson (May 2025): AI still handles about two-thirds of customer inquiries; response times improved 82% since launch; repeat issues down 25%. "AI gives us speed. Talent gives us empathy." "But in a world of automation, nothing is more valuable than a truly great human interaction."

sources.title: Klarna changes its AI tune and again recruits humans for customer service

claims.notes: This shows the AI was not switched off. Klarna framed the move as the "next level" of its AI-led strategy, not a reversal. Media outlets (e.g. Silicon Canals "U-turn", tech.co "reverses") framed it as a reversal; that is interpretation.

claims.claim: Klarna priced its US IPO at $40 per share (above the $35-37 range). It began trading on the NYSE as "KLAR" on 2025-09-10 at a valuation of about $15 billion.

sources.title: Klarna Announces Pricing of its Initial Public Offering
Klarna raises USD 1.37 billion in US IPO

claims.notes: The valuation is reported as ~$15B or ~$15.2B depending on the outlet. First-day closing price differs by source ($45.82 per AP/IPOScoop vs $46.40 per Crunchbase). Verified from search snippets; the Business Wire release was not fetched in full.

claims.claim: Q3 2025 earnings call: Siemiatkowski said the AI assistant "can now do the work of more than 853 full-time agents" (up from 700) and has saved the company $60 million. "We continue to see very demonstrable value from Klarna's AI assistant." Customer service and operations cost was $50M in Q3 2025 vs $42M a year earlier.

sources.title: Klarna says AI agent does the work of 853 employees

claims.notes: This is the key later update: Klarna doubled down on AI after the May 2025 pivot. The FTE-equivalence and savings figures are unaudited. The rising customer service cost line (from CX Dive) complicates the savings story; interpret with care. The exact earnings call date was not verified (the article was published Nov 20, 2025).

claims.claim: At Charter's Leading with AI Summit (2026-02-10), Siemiatkowski said: "We actually are rethinking this. We're going to use AI to support humans and also support the simplest [tasks]" and "we think it's going to be like the future to offer human support—it's going to be like the VIP treatment". The article also says the AI agent does the equivalent work of 850 agents, that headcount is down ~50% via attrition since 2022, and that revenue per employee rose from $300K to $1.3M.

sources.title: What Klarna Learned from its Ambitious AI Rollout

claims.notes: This is sponsored partner content by Charter, not TIME editorial, so weigh accordingly. The headcount and revenue-per-employee figures are the CEO's claims and are unaudited. This is the most recent statement found. Some blogs date the "VIP" remark to 2025 or June 2026; the Charter piece dates it to Feb 2026.

claims.claim: Forrester analyst Kate Leggett said Klarna "overpivoted on their AI strategy".

sources.title: Klarna says AI agent does the work of 853 employees

claims.notes: This is a third-party analyst view and is optional context. Seen via search snippet of the CX Dive piece.

open_questions: The full text of the Bloomberg 2025-05-08 interview could not be accessed (paywall/403). The quotes were verified only via secondary outlets citing it (CX Dive, The Independent, CX Today, Entrepreneur).

The F-1 text on sec.gov was not read directly. The headcount figures (5,527 -> 3,422) come from CNBC's reading of the prospectus. I did not verify whether the F-1 repeats the 700-agent or two-thirds claims.
How many in-house human agents Klarna eventually hired under the 'Uber-type' pilot is unknown. The only number found is two (May 2025).
No independent or audited verification exists of the 700/853/850 FTE-equivalence, the 11->2 minute resolution time, CSAT parity, the $40M estimate or the $60M savings.
Whether the 2024 '700 agents' corresponded to actual job losses is unclear. Klarna's agents were largely outsourced, and no source documents 700 layoffs.
Whether there was any Klarna statement after Feb 2026 (through Oct 2026) on AI customer service; none was found in this search pass.
The 'two-thirds' share (Klarna) vs '75%' (Entrepreneur) discrepancy: Klarna's primary wording is two-thirds.

timeline.event: Klarna pauses most hiring as it invests in AI (per CEO, Dec 2024).
OpenAI-powered AI assistant goes live globally.
Klarna press release: 2.3M conversations, two-thirds of chats, equivalent of 700 full-time agents, <2 min vs 11 min, $40M estimated profit improvement; humans still available.
CEO says Klarna stopped hiring a year ago; headcount down 22% to ~3,500.
Bloomberg interview: CEO says cost focus led to 'lower quality'; customers should always be able to reach a human; Uber-type in-house human agent pilot.
Klarna spokesperson: AI still handles ~two-thirds of inquiries; 'AI gives us speed. Talent gives us empathy.'
CNBC: CEO says company shrank from ~5,000 to almost 3,000 employees, partly through attrition.
Klarna lists on NYSE (KLAR), priced at $40, ~$15B valuation.
CEO: AI assistant now does the work of 853+ agents and has saved $60M.
Charter summit: CEO says human support will be 'like the VIP treatment'; AI for the simplest tasks and to support humans.
